A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same SFTMix paper. Their methods, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original SFTMix-versus-NTP experiments on instruction-following and medical benchmarks, together with ablations and detailed results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and reports additional human preferences, data-selection comparisons, LoRA experiments, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: v2 Section 5.6 adds a LoRA-based SFTMix training variant, whereas v1 leaves parameter-efficient integration as future work. The default confidence split, tokenwise interpolation, and combined NTP-plus-Mixup objective remain unchanged. Explicitly separating hidden representations from the linear output head is an equivalent reformulation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same instruction-following and medical datasets and benchmarks, including the GPT-4 replacement responses used in the data-quality analysis. Human evaluation uses an existing AlpacaEval-2 subset; selection experiments change sampling, and LoRA changes training configuration, without adding task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 newly evaluates AlpaGasus and Long selection pipelines with NTP and SFTMix; these methods were only cited in v1. Table 6 also adds NTP-only controls on confident and unconfident subsets. This substantially broadens the supplementary comparisons, while retaining the main NTP and five biomedical-model comparators.

E3.justification: v2 introduces human pairwise evaluation using 80 Vicuna instructions and 200 judgments, with evaluators instructed to disregard response length (Appendix B.2). It also adds experiments using 1,000 selected training examples and LoRA versus full-parameter tuning. The original training epochs, optimizer settings, and three-shot medical evaluation remain documented.

E4.justification: The four original ablation directions are retained and reorganized. v2 adds matched subset controls without Mixup, data-selection and LoRA compatibility analyses, reported regularization-weight sensitivity results, and a topic audit of the 50 most and 50 least confident examples. v1's MT-Bench extraction case study is removed.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix A Tables 4–5 report standard errors for the main instruction-following and medical comparisons. v2 removes these uncertainty reports without replacements. Five instruction-following evaluation rounds and three medical evaluation rounds remain stated; the reporting loss does not establish fewer runs.

E6.justification: All mean values in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged, and v1 Table 3's ablation values are retained across v2 Tables 3–6. v2 adds subset-control, selection, LoRA, hyperparameter, and topic-analysis results, plus human preferences of 42.5% for SFTMix, 26.5% for NTP, and 31% ties. v1's category-level scores and extraction example are removed.

T1.justification: New Appendix A derives the Mixup gradient through the linear head and softmax, arguing that it generally changes the NTP gradient direction rather than merely reweighting original examples. v1 has no corresponding derivation. The central loss mathematics is retained, while v1's explicit formula for Perpc is omitted.

C1.justification: The central claim of improving instruction-following and medical SFT through confidence-guided Mixup remains. v2 adds explicit contribution claims about data-selection compatibility and compute-constrained training. Its abstract also replaces v1's claim about datasets of any size with the more bounded wording of varying sizes and qualities.

C2.justification: v2 adds the gradient-modification interpretation and discusses the new evidence for compatibility with data selection and LoRA. Section 7 newly acknowledges English-only evaluation and untested safety alignment. The existing limitations concerning pretraining and larger LLMs are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies balanced confidence batches, random pairing, the regularization-weight search grid, and human-rating instructions. It omits v1's explicit gradient-accumulation and Alpaca prompt/template descriptions and identifies the judge less precisely as GPT-4 rather than GPT-4-Turbo. These documentation changes do not establish changed underlying settings; LoRA-specific hyperparameters are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds CommonIT and importance-based data-selection references, citations supporting its margin/overfitting motivation, and safety-evaluation references. It removes the QLoRA and original AlpacaEval citations. The broader positioning around instruction tuning, data cartography, and Mixup remains unchanged; publication-metadata updates do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition, and experimental descriptions are extensively rewritten or condensed. The method is reorganized into preliminaries, motivation, and a three-step recipe; analysis sections are reordered, limitations receive a separate section, and the appendix structure is replaced.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a single-column to a two-column layout. The pipeline diagram is revised, the confidence boxplot is redrawn horizontally, and the example panel and extraction figure are removed. The combined ablation table is split into Tables 3–6, Tables 7–9 are added, and the original appendix tables disappear.

improvement.justification: The added subset controls and human comparisons strengthen support for SFTMix, while the LoRA/selection analyses, gradient explanation, and explicit limitations improve its assessment. These provide a limited net benefit. The unchanged main results gain supporting evidence, but removing v1 Appendix A's standard errors and category breakdown weakens transparency, and the new LoRA experiment remains sparsely specified.
